svg.title: Cycle diagram of the lecture's account of bipolar disorder: early life stress causes HPA axis dysfunction, which triggers dysregulation of dopamine circuits. Mania (too much dopamine) leads, through a compensatory response that lowers dopamine receptor sensitivity, to depression-like symptoms (too little dopamine), and a compensatory response swings activity back the other way to mania. Below the cycle, serotonin is decreased in both manic and depressive periods.
